arguments.text: Fixed: `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js. The year 0–99 workaround shifted the year by 1900, which misaligns the leap years (1900+99=1999 vs year 99, 1900+100=2000 vs year 100), so `plus` was a day off when a day-based addition crossed Feb 29 of the intermediate 19XX/20XX year. It now shifts by 400 years (the Gregorian cycle), so leap years line up: `0099-12-31 + 61d` = `0100-03-02` (agrees with `fromObject({year:100,month:3,day:2})`), `0000-02-29` is representable, and `0099-12-31 + 2d` = `0100-01-02` still holds. Full suite: only the 2 pre-existing fr-locale failures remain.

Fixed: `DateTime#isInDST` in src/datetime.js compared the current offset against `set({ month: 1 })` / `set({ month: 5 })`, i.e. the same day-of-month, so for the 1974 US year-round DST the January reference was itself in DST and it returned false for most of 1974. It now compares against Jan 1 and May 1: in 1974 America/New_York it is true from Jan 6 (after the 2am transition) through Oct 27 and false outside that window; 1975 and southern-hemisphere zones still behave correctly, and the existing isInDST tests pass.

Fixed: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js now pads negative numbers correctly (sign first, then the absolute value padded to n digits), so `toISODate()`/`toISO()`/`toFormat("yyyy")` render negative years as `-0005-05-25` instead of `00-5-05-25`. Large negative years (`-118040-05-25`) and positive years are unchanged, and the full suite still passes apart from the 2 pre-existing fr-locale failures.

Fixed: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js always returned true; it now returns `isNumber(this.fixed) && !isNaN(this.fixed)`. So `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp").isValid` is false and a DateTime set to such a zone is invalid ("unsupported zone"), while `utcInstance`, `instance(n)` and `parseSpecifier("UTC+6")` stay valid.
